transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-16 10:00 UTC
Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake, Priya Kapoor, Ethan Park, Sofia Ramirez, Emily Chen, Ava Martinez + All staff (by registration)

[00:00] Jordan Blake: Good morning everyone, thanks for joining the April all-hands. Quick housekeep - recording is on, we'll keep this to about an hour plus Q&A.
[00:25] Jordan Blake: First thing - big thanks for Q1. Numbers are mixed but overall solid, we grew hosted usage by ~38% q/q, Dedicated renewals stayed healthy. There were some regressions on latency p95 for a subset of customers, we'll cover that.
[01:10] Priya Kapoor: Hi all - I'm Priya. I'll go through product highlights. Quick note: the new KV cache rollout cut token costs by up to, uh, 12% in alpha, with better cold-start latency. Caveat - we saw a regression on some long-context models when autoscaling triggered, that's a bug we're tracking.
[02:05] Ethan Park: On the product side, Q2 focus is three areas: 1) serving runtime optimizations (kernel selection improvements), 2) Dedicated autoscaling policies and burst capacity, and 3) Private deployment automation for enterprise onprem customers.
[02:45] Jordan Blake: Can you elaborate on kernel selection? There's been some confusion.
[02:50] Priya Kapoor: Yeah, so our scheduler now picks kernels based on model arch + seq len distribution. More heuristics, less brute force. Should help tail latency. We still need per-customer profiles, which we'll add.
[03:20] Sofia Ramirez: On infra - we've rolled out a hotfix to prevent the KV cache eviction race condition. We've also started a bench run of optimized CUDA kernels on our staging fleet. Early results show 8-14% token throughput improvement on long-form generation.
[04:10] Audience Member (Mic off): Sorry can you repeat the numbers?
[04:15] Sofia Ramirez: 8 to 14% throughput on the specific long-seq bench. Not universal.
[05:00] Jordan Blake: Sales & GTM - Emily?
[05:05] Emily Chen: We're seeing stronger inbound from AI-native startups and mid-market SaaS. Big push on enterprise renewals this quarter, focusing on Dedicated and Private. We closed two Dedicated deals in EMEA last month, pipeline looks healthy. Reminder: when customers ask about vendor lock-in vs. openness, lean into our unified API and migration support.
[06:00] Jordan Blake: Security update - short note on SOC 2.
[06:05] Priya Kapoor (covering security): We're on track for SOC 2 Type II evaluation in Q3. Security team has completed the third-party audit for our logging pipeline, working on encryption-at-rest key rotation docs. We'll publish an FAQ for customers.
[06:45] Jordan Blake: On product pricing - small pricing tweak for embeddings churn we're testing with a handful of users, not broad yet.
[07:05] Ethan Park: Regarding refunds and credits: for the subset affected by the latency regression, Customer Success has offered credits and is running asynchronous benchmarks with a couple of customers.
[07:40] Jordan Blake: Hiring & org priorities - Ava?
[07:45] Ava Martinez: Hiring plan - headcount is approved for 18 hires in Q2: 9 engineers, 4 product/PM, 3 sales/AM, 2 support. Managers, please begin backfills and prioritize infra/serving roles. We'll run a hiring calibration session next week.
[08:25] Jordan Blake: Questions from the team - pls drop them in the Q&A so we can triage.
[08:35] Q1 (pre-submitted) - Will we expand in APAC?
[08:40] Jordan Blake: Yes, region expansion roadmap includes Singapore region later this year; exact timing depends on demand and partner integrations.
[09:10] Q2 - Are we open-sourcing any components?
[09:15] Priya Kapoor: We're evaluating a few non-core libs (observability helpers, benchmark harness) for community release later in the year. Main runtime remains productized.
[09:45] Live Q&A - [10:00] Speaker 1: On Dedicated SLAs, can we see more granular SLOs per route?
[10:05] Emily Chen: We're piloting per-route latency tiers for a set of enterprise customers; it'll be part of the Dedicated offering add-on.
[10:35] Speaker 2: For Private (on-prem) - what are the network requirements?
[10:40] Priya Kapoor: VPC peering or private link is supported; we have an on-prem package that can run air-gapped but with extra setup. We'll share the network checklist after the call.
[11:20] Jordan Blake: Finance snapshot - short: burn is as expected, runway into late 2027 with current plan. We are tracking unit economics closely - our Optimize toolkit is starting to show improvements in cost per token for big customers.
[12:00] Ethan Park: A quick demo highlight - we shipped function/tool-calling improvements for structured outputs, better reliability for retrying external tool calls. This solves a bunch of customer pain points where JSON output would truncate.
[12:45] Jordan Blake: Customer stories - shoutouts to the EMEA customer that moved to Dedicated and reported 30% cost savings with our batching and cache profile.
[13:20] Jordan Blake: Closing - recap of next steps: Priya publishes product roadmap/OKRs, Security sends SOC2 FAQ, Managers run hiring calibration; Customer Success to follow up on the latency-impacted accounts.
[13:40] Jordan Blake: Thanks everyone, we'll post recording and slides. Office hours next Tuesday for deeper Q&A.
[13:55] End of recording.
